_method_version: 1.0.0 publishes nine figures on one API. A tenth was built and cut: it drew the same per-year method series as figure 7 and asserted “different objects” by printing two medians side by side, which figures 8 and 9 measure properly by crossing the axes. Five figures shipped first as ranked bar lists with the counts printed beside the bars; re-encoding them was meant to be presentation work and instead produced four new findings and two corrections, both of which are kept visible on the plates rather than quietly fixed.

source.licence: PDB data are released into the public domain (CC0); RCSB asks for citation.
source.note: Live and additive; the register grows weekly, so every figure is a statement about one fetch. Counts are entries, not distinct proteins. Nothing is downloaded in bulk: five fetch phases issue about two hundred faceted queries and assemble one cache.

screens.same query twice: 260,089 both times, stable within a session
screens.a nonsense value: HTTP 204, zero results, not the unfiltered total
screens.deposit date vs release date: differ by up to 2,203 entries a year
screens.terms facet ordering: returns the top N by count but NOT in count order: 35 of 200 accessions arrive out of sequence, so anything positional must sort first

cache.note: Not a source download. This is the assembled result of the five fetch phases, recorded so a forker can tell whether their refetch reproduced the published figures.

corrections_on_the_published_plates: Figure 7 previously listed a scenario in which the deceleration continues and cryo-EM levels off below X-ray, offered as evidence the forecast was wide. It was asserted and never computed, and it is wrong: the decay still compounds to about 4.2x the 2024 level and crosses in 2027. Computing it narrowed the forecast instead of widening it.
Figure 6 previously read 87% at 100 K off a histogram bucket, which is everything in [100, 125) K, 173,631 entries. The exact terms value is 166,568.
Figure 3 plotted the accession facet in the order the API returned it on an axis labelled rank. Sorting first moves the rank-size fit from R2 0.77 to 0.88.
A cryo-EM share was quoted as 42.7% against an unstated base of two methods; it is 41.8% of all depositions, and the base is now named.
